question: Following the takeover of Mediobanca by the bank Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS), the Italian judiciary opened an enquiry into market manipulation, obstruction of supervision and collusion between the shareholders concerned with the endorsement of the government. MPS was rescued in 2017 using vast sums of Italian public money, and the judiciary is also investigating the murky acquisition of a 15 % share in MPS sold by the Ministry of Economy and Finance in November 2014. In the light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission still not consider it necessary to intervene, at least as a precautionary measure, at the risk of appearing complicit, in the eyes of the public, with the private groups who clubbed together to take over Mediobanca and with the Italian Government which gave them its blessing for this, in breach of EU rules on the neutrality of public entities vis-à-vis financial institutions1?

What immediate checks will it conduct to ensure that the opacity of the MPS takeover of Mediobanca has not compromised the sound and prudent management of credit institutions required under the Capital Requirements Directive2?

How is it ensuring that the MPS-Mediobanca transaction does not constitute a distortion of competition and a subsequent or indirect infringement of the Community framework for State aid3, even though MPS is no longer prohibited from acquiring other entities?
Article 345 TFEU CRD Articles 22 and 23. Article 107 TFEU
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.1.2026) The Commission is closely monitoring the developments in the Italian banking sector, including the takeover of Mediobanca by Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) to ensure that it complies with applicable EU law.

However, the Commission is not responsible for supervising the sound and prudent management of individual credit institutions or the transparency of specific takeovers pursuant to capital markets legislation.

These matters are within the remit of competent authorities, such as the Single Supervisory Mechanism and Commissione Nazionale per le Societa’ e la Borsa (CONSOB), which are responsible for ensuring compliance with the Capital Requirements Directive1, the Takeover Bids Directive2, and other relevant EU legislation.

As regards the Commission State aid decisions3, following the expiry of its commitment to refrain from acquisitions, MPS was enabled to undertake the corporate actions deemed appropriate to pursue its own business interests in the course of 2025, including the tender offer over Mediobanca. That transaction was not notifiable to the Commission under the EU merger control rules4, as the thresholds were not met.
However, it had to be notified to the Italian competition authority, which approved it from a merger control perspective in July 2025.
1 OJ L 176, 27.6.2013, pp. 338–436. 2 OJ L 142, 30.4.2004, pp. 12–23. 3 Commission decision 4690 of 4 July 2017, OJ C 40, 2.2.2018, p. 1, as modified by the Commission decision
6525 of 12 September 2019, OJ C 7, 10.1.2020, p. 2, and the Commission decision 5536 of 2 August 2022, OJ C 387, 7.10.2022. 4 OJ L 24, 29.1.2004, pp. 1–22.
